summary:
swyx opens by reviewing three years of keynote themes: AI productivity gains, declining AI costs (~100x per 12–18 months), and 'tiny teams' (companies with more millions in revenue than employees). AI Engineer is a tiny team of 9 full-time people generating over $9M. After joining Cognition, swyx added Devin to their previously non-AI stack (Figma, React, Supabase, Google Sheets, Sessionize). A designer's Figma page expected to take weeks was implemented pixel-perfect overnight. swyx emphasizes agents eliminate 'yak shaving'—dependency installation, Python fixes, tree crawling—and that a productivity model must appreciate parallelism, not just autonomy. Usage exploded: threads hit 207 and 127 replies. A non-technical designer independently annotated Devin with red-line instructions TLDraw-style. swyx's key insight: employees produce more work because feedback cycles are instant and blocking is gone.

The 2026 theme is 'agents for everything else.' Devin manages the conference schedule as code (replacing a CMS), handles speaker changes via forwarded emails, performs ETL from external vendor APIs, and even researched and purchased a lobster. Town Assistant converts Apple Notes into formatted Notion docs with speaker research. swyx argues coding agents will break containment into knowledge management—a top 3–5 trend for 2026.

In the final section, swyx addresses replacing entire SaaS tools with custom agent-built alternatives, acknowledging he has 'the most psychosis' and must manage valid employee concerns. His method: identify the top three concerns and systematically reduce them. He references Malte's Vercel keynote noting 60% of Vercel's user base is now bots, meaning APIs, CLIs, and MCPs matter more than dashboards. MCP speakers Edo and Liad argue custom UI is going away—ship to someone else's app. This shift toward 'agent experience' means swyx no longer cares about Figma dashboards. He closes with a call to action: 'agents for everything else are coming. Wake up. Use it. Bring it home to work.'
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Keynote History
sections.summary: swyx fills in for the UK Chief AI Officer and reviews three years of keynote themes: AI productivity gains, declining AI costs (~100x per 12–18 months), and tiny teams (more millions in revenue than employees). AI Engineer itself is a tiny team of 9 people generating over $9M.

sections.title: From Non-AI Stack to Devin
sections.summary: AI Engineer's stack was non-AI (Figma, React, Supabase, Tido, Google Sheets, Sessionize). After joining Cognition, swyx added Devin to Slack. A designer's Figma page expected to take weeks was implemented pixel-perfect overnight. Lesson: agents save yak shaves—dependency crawling, Python fixes—emphasizing parallelism not just autonomy.

sections.title: Exploding Usage and Human Productivity
sections.summary: Devin threads hit 207 and 127 replies. A non-technical designer in Indonesia independently used red-line annotations TLDraw-style with no instruction manual. swyx added an Easter egg and tweet-inspired design via Devin. Key insight: employees produce more work because feedback cycles are instant and blocking is gone—animations, polish, things never before received.

sections.title: Agents for Everything Else
sections.summary: The conference is a giant data management problem: 130 speakers, dozens of sponsors. swyx replaced the CMS with code as source of truth, letting Devin manage the schedule. Speaker changes are handled by forwarding emails to Devin. 9 people manage 1000 attendees; 6000 planned for San Francisco. Agents also handle ETL from external vendor APIs.

sections.title: Agents for Buying and Town Assistant
sections.summary: Devin researched and facilitated purchasing a lobster for the conference after a viral tweet inspired swyx. swyx demos Town Assistant converting Apple Notes into a formatted Notion doc with speaker research. He argues coding agents will break containment into knowledge management—a top 3–5 trend for 2026, referencing Andrej Karpathy's wiki concept.

sections.title: SaaS Replacement, Agent Experience, and Call to Action
sections.summary: swyx discusses replacing entire SaaS tools with custom agent-built alternatives, acknowledging his enthusiasm as 'psychosis' and the need to manage valid employee concerns by identifying and systematically reducing the top three. He references Malte's Vercel keynote noting 60% of Vercel's user base is now bots, meaning APIs, CLIs, and MCPs matter more than dashboards. MCP speakers Edo and Liad argue custom UI is going away—ship to someone else's app. This shift toward 'agent experience' means swyx no longer cares about Figma dashboards, throwing designs into cloud co-work. He closes: 'agents for everything else are coming. Wake up. Use it. Bring it home to work.'

limitations: swyx initially mistrusted Devin's marketing claims until seeing results firsthand.
Hooking Devin to Figma required a separate tool (Coworker) for integration.
swyx is not the biggest fan of Sanity CMS, prompting the move to code-as-source-of-truth.
swyx acknowledges employee concerns about AI replacing SaaS are valid and must be systematically addressed, not dismissed.
Adopting AI aggressively can feel like 'psychosis'—managers must bring employees along the journey without talking down to them.
